Save Our Planet

Eco-Awareness Chapter 7

Learn how to report environmental facts, read simple data, use scientific terms, and persuade people to take small but meaningful actions for a cleaner school, a healthier coast, and a safer planet.

Text TypesReport Text & Exposition Text
Language FocusTechnical Terms, Present Passive Voice, Generalizing Words
Final ProductObservation Report or Eco-Action Presentation

Essential Questions

  • What environmental problems can we observe around our school and island?
  • How can scientific facts help us explain environmental problems?
  • How can we use English to report facts and persuade people to take action?
A. Chapter Overview

Welcome to Chapter 7

Student-facing material

Bayangkan suatu pagi setelah angin kencang. Kamu berjalan menuju kelas dan melihat beberapa gelas plastik, bungkus makanan, dan botol minuman berserakan di halaman sekolah. Sebagian sampah tersangkut di selokan. Sebagian lagi terbawa angin ke arah jalan dan mungkin akhirnya sampai ke laut.

Situasi seperti ini bukan hanya masalah kebersihan. Ini juga berhubungan dengan kesehatan, kebiasaan siswa, kehidupan laut, pekerjaan nelayan, rumput laut, pantai, dan masa depan lingkungan kepulauan.

Learning Goals

  1. Understand Report Text and Exposition Text about environmental issues.
  2. Identify technical terms, generalizing words, and present passive voice.
  3. Read simple environmental data and use it as evidence.
  4. Write a short observation report and a short exposition text.
  5. Present an eco-action plan clearly and confidently.
Final Product: At the end of this chapter, you will create a School Cleanliness Observation Report, a Class Eco-Action Plan, or a Plastic Waste Reduction Campaign.

C–E. Key Concepts

Report Text and Exposition Text

What Is a Report Text?

A Report Text is a text that presents factual information about a general subject. It explains what something is, what it is like, what parts it has, or how it happens.

Dalam Bahasa Indonesia, Report Text adalah teks yang menyajikan informasi faktual tentang suatu hal secara umum. Teks ini tidak berfokus pada pengalaman pribadi, tetapi pada fakta yang dapat diamati atau dijelaskan.

Social Function

To describe or explain a general phenomenon based on facts.

StructureFunctionExample
General ClassificationIntroduces the topic or classifies the subject.Plastic waste is a type of waste made from synthetic materials.
DescriptionDescribes features, types, causes, effects, or data.It is commonly found in schools, beaches, rivers, and coastal areas.

What Is an Exposition Text?

An Exposition Text is a text that presents an opinion or argument about an issue. The writer gives reasons and evidence to persuade readers.

Dalam Bahasa Indonesia, Exposition Text adalah teks yang berisi pendapat, alasan, dan bukti untuk meyakinkan pembaca tentang suatu isu.

Social Function

To persuade readers that an idea, action, or opinion is important.

StructureFunctionExample
ThesisStates the writer’s opinion.Students should reduce single-use plastic at school.
ArgumentsGives reasons and evidence.First, plastic waste can pollute the school and the sea.
RecommendationRestates the opinion and suggests action.Therefore, students should bring tumblers.

Report Text vs Exposition Text

AspectReport TextExposition Text
PurposeTo explain facts about something.To persuade readers about an idea.
Main QuestionWhat is it like?Why should we care or act?
ToneObjective and factual.Persuasive and argumentative.
StructureGeneral Classification + Description.Thesis + Arguments + Recommendation.
Example TitlePlastic Waste in Coastal AreasStudents Should Reduce Single-Use Plastic
Language FocusTechnical terms, simple present, passive voice.Opinion, reasons, connectors, recommendation.
Don’t Get Confused: Report Text explains facts. Exposition Text argues a position. Report Text answers “What is it like?” Exposition Text answers “Why should we care or act?”

G–H. Model Texts

Read, Notice, and Analyze

Model Text 1 — Report Text

Plastic Waste in Coastal School Areas

General Classification

Plastic waste is a type of non-biodegradable waste made from synthetic materials. It is commonly used for bottles, cups, straws, bags, food wrappers, and packaging. In many schools, plastic waste is one of the most visible environmental problems because students often buy snacks and drinks in plastic containers.

Description

In coastal school areas, plastic waste can easily move from the school yard to drainage systems, roads, beaches, and the sea. Light plastic items such as snack wrappers and plastic bags are often carried by wind. Plastic bottles and cups may block drainage when they are not thrown into proper bins.

A simple school observation was conducted near the canteen, corridor, and school yard for 30 minutes. The observation found 18 plastic cups, 12 food wrappers, 9 plastic bottles, 7 pieces of paper, and 5 organic waste items. The data shows that plastic cups were found the most. This indicates that drink packaging is a common source of waste at school.

Plastic waste can affect the school environment and coastal life. Dirty areas can create an uncomfortable learning space. Blocked drainage can cause puddles after rain. If plastic waste reaches the sea, it may harm fish, coral reefs, and other marine life. Therefore, plastic waste management is important for students, schools, and coastal communities.

Text Structure Analysis

StructureParagraphExplanation
General ClassificationParagraph 1Introduces plastic waste and classifies it as non-biodegradable waste.
DescriptionParagraph 2Describes how plastic waste moves in coastal school areas.
DescriptionParagraph 3Presents observation data.
DescriptionParagraph 4Explains the impact of plastic waste.

Model Text 2 — Exposition Text

Students Should Reduce Single-Use Plastic

Thesis

Students should reduce single-use plastic at school because it creates waste, harms the environment, and affects coastal life.

Argument 1

First, single-use plastic is usually used only once, but it can stay in the environment for a long time. Plastic cups, straws, snack wrappers, and plastic bags are often thrown away after break time. When many students use single-use plastic every day, the amount of waste increases quickly.

Argument 2

Second, plastic waste can move from school areas to drainage, rivers, beaches, and the sea. This is a serious problem for students in coastal areas because the sea is part of daily life. Many families depend on clean seas for fish, seaweed, transportation, and income.

Argument 3

Third, reducing plastic is possible through simple habits. Students can bring tumblers, use reusable lunch boxes, refuse plastic straws, and throw waste into proper bins. These actions are small, but they can reduce waste and build responsibility.

Recommendation

Therefore, students should start reducing single-use plastic now. A clean school begins with small habits. If every class takes part, the school environment will become cleaner, healthier, and more comfortable for learning.

Structure Analysis

StructureContent
ThesisStudents should reduce single-use plastic at school.
Argument 1Single-use plastic creates more waste.
Argument 2Plastic waste can move to the sea and affect coastal life.
Argument 3Students can reduce plastic through simple habits.
RecommendationStudents should start reducing single-use plastic now.

I. Reading Section

Why Mangroves Matter for Coastal Communities

General Classification

Mangroves are trees or shrubs that grow in coastal areas, especially in muddy and salty water. They are part of an important coastal ecosystem. Mangroves can be found near beaches, river mouths, and shallow coastal waters.

Description

Mangroves have special roots that help them survive in wet and salty areas. Their roots can hold soil and reduce coastal erosion. In many coastal communities, mangroves help protect the land from strong waves and wind.

Mangroves are also important for marine life. Many small fish, crabs, shrimp, and other sea animals use mangrove roots as a safe place to live and grow. When mangrove areas are healthy, the coastal ecosystem becomes stronger.

Mangroves also support people’s lives. Coastal communities often depend on fish, crabs, and other marine resources. If mangrove areas are damaged, marine life may lose its habitat, and people may lose part of their natural protection.

However, mangroves can be threatened by pollution, careless cutting, land conversion, and plastic waste. Plastic bags and bottles may get trapped among mangrove roots. This can make the area dirty and disturb young plants.

Therefore, mangrove conservation is important. Students can help by joining clean-up activities, learning about coastal ecosystems, reducing plastic waste, and sharing information with their friends and families.

K. Speaking Section

Discuss and Present Eco-Actions

Dialogue Model

Alya: Look at the school yard. There are many plastic cups near the canteen.

Rafi: Yes, I noticed that too. I think our school has a plastic waste problem.

Alya: In my opinion, students should bring tumblers.

Rafi: That’s a good idea. The data from our class observation also shows that plastic cups were found the most.

Alya: Why don’t we start a “Bring Your Tumbler Day”?

Rafi: I agree. We can also make posters to remind students.

Alya: We should explain the reason clearly. Plastic waste can move to the drainage and the sea.

Rafi: Yes. Let’s present this idea to our class.

Alya: Great. Small actions can make our school cleaner.

M–O. Grammar Focus

Technical Terms, Passive Voice, and Generalizing Words

Grammar Focus 1 — Technical Terms

Technical terms are special words used in a specific field. In this chapter, the field is environmental science.

ecosystemmicroplasticsbiodegradablenon-biodegradablegreenhouse gasescarbon dioxidemangroveconservation

Grammar Focus 2 — Present Passive Voice

Active: People throw plastic waste into the drainage.

Passive: Plastic waste is thrown into the drainage.

Formula: Subject + am/is/are + past participle + complement

Grammar Focus 3 — Generalizing Words

Generalizing words are used to make statements about groups, habits, or common situations.

manymostsomeseveralin generalusuallyoftenrarely

School Waste Observation

Observe • Record • Report • Act
Observation Focus

Use the Picture as Your Mini Lab Model

Gambar ini menunjukkan cara kerja kelompok saat melakukan observasi: ada siswa yang mencatat data, ada yang menghitung jenis sampah, dan ada yang mendokumentasikan area pengamatan.

  • Observe: look carefully at one school area.
  • Record: count the waste items and write the data.
  • Report: turn the data into factual English sentences.
  • Act: propose one realistic eco-action for your class.
Sentence model: The data shows that plastic cups were found the most.

Purpose

  1. Observe waste around your school.
  2. Record simple data.
  3. Describe the data in English.
  4. Write a short report text.
  5. Propose one realistic eco-action.
Safety Note: Do not touch dangerous waste directly. If you find broken glass, sharp metal, medical waste, or unknown liquid, report it to your teacher or school staff.

Tools and Areas

Tools: notebook, pen, observation table, gloves if available, phone camera if allowed, waste bag if supervised.

Observation Areas: classroom, corridor, canteen area, school yard, school gate, drainage near school, beach or road near school if safe and supervised.

Steps

  1. Choose one observation area.
  2. Observe the area for 10–15 minutes.
  3. Count visible waste items.
  4. Record the data in the table.
  5. Discuss possible causes.
  6. Write three factual sentences using the data.
  7. Write one passive sentence.
  8. Write one recommendation.
  9. Present your finding to the class.

Data Sentence Examples

SentenceArti Bahasa Indonesia
The observation was conducted near the canteen.Observasi dilakukan di dekat kantin.
Twelve plastic cups were found in the area.Dua belas gelas plastik ditemukan di area tersebut.
Food wrappers were found near the school yard.Bungkus makanan ditemukan di dekat halaman sekolah.
The data shows that plastic cups were the most common waste.Data menunjukkan bahwa gelas plastik adalah sampah yang paling umum.
The problem may be caused by careless habits after break time.Masalah itu mungkin disebabkan oleh kebiasaan kurang peduli setelah jam istirahat.

Reflection Questions

  1. What type of waste was found the most?
  2. Why do you think it happened?
  3. Who should be responsible for solving the problem?
  4. What action is realistic for your class?
  5. What English sentence can describe your data?
Q–S. Interactive Quiz

Multiple Choice A–E, Essay, and True/False

Multiple Choice Questions — LOTS, MOTS, HOTS

Pilih A, B, C, D, atau E. Soal dirancang seperti situasi nyata agar kamu berpikir, bukan hanya menghafal.

LOTSQuestion 1

During English class, Nisa reads a text about plastic waste. The text begins by defining plastic waste as non-biodegradable material. Then, it explains the types, examples, and impacts of plastic waste in coastal areas.

What type of text is Nisa reading?

LOTSQuestion 2

A group writes this sentence in their report: “Plastic waste is commonly found near the canteen after break time.”

Which language feature is shown by the phrase “is commonly found”?

LOTSQuestion 3

Raka wants to write a scientific word for “tiny plastic particles that can pollute water.”

Which word should he use?

LOTSQuestion 4

In an exposition text, the part that states the writer’s opinion at the beginning is called ...

Choose the correct text-structure term.

LOTSQuestion 5

Look at the sentence: “Many students buy drinks in plastic cups during break time.”

The word “many” is used as ...

MOTSQuestion 6

A class observes the canteen area for 15 minutes. They find 14 plastic cups, 10 food wrappers, 6 plastic bottles, and 3 pieces of paper. They want to write one factual sentence for a report text.

Which sentence is the best?

MOTSQuestion 7

Sinta writes this paragraph: “Students should bring tumblers to school. First, tumblers can reduce plastic cup waste. Second, students can save money because they do not always need to buy drinks in plastic cups. Therefore, bringing tumblers is a simple eco-habit.”

What is the purpose of the paragraph?

MOTSQuestion 8

A student wants to write a passive sentence about a weekly plastic bottle collection program.

Which sentence is written in correct present passive voice?

MOTSQuestion 9

A group wants to write an exposition text about waste sorting. They already have this thesis: “Students should sort waste at school.”

Which argument best supports the thesis?

MOTSQuestion 10

Read the sentence: “The drainage is blocked by plastic bottles and food wrappers after heavy rain.”

What problem is described in the sentence?

HOTSQuestion 11

Your group observes the school yard and finds this data: plastic cups 20, food wrappers 18, plastic bottles 9, paper 4, organic waste 3. You want to make a recommendation based on the data.

Which recommendation is the most logical?

HOTSQuestion 12

A student writes this report sentence: “Plastic waste is bad. It is very, very bad. Everyone knows it is bad.”

The sentence is weak because ...

HOTSQuestion 13

A group wants to persuade students to stop littering after break time. They need one strong exposition paragraph with opinion, evidence, reason, and recommendation.

Which exposition paragraph is the strongest?

HOTSQuestion 14

A student writes this sentence: “Students throw plastic cups near the canteen.” The teacher asks the student to focus on the object, not the doer.

Which revision is correct?

HOTSQuestion 15

Your class wants to start an environmental campaign, but some students say, “It will not make any difference.”

Which response is the most persuasive and realistic?

Essay Questions

  1. Read a short report text about plastic waste. Identify the General Classification and Description parts.
    Write your answer here.
  2. Write two arguments for this thesis: “Students should sort waste at school.”
    Write your answer here.
  3. Change these active sentences into passive voice: a. Students clean the school yard. b. The class records the data. c. People plant mangroves near the beach.
    Write your answer here.
  4. Write three sentences using this data: Plastic cups 15, Food wrappers 11, Plastic bottles 8.
    Write your answer here.
  5. Design one eco-action plan for your class. Explain the problem, action, and expected result.
    Write your answer here.

ClarityEasy to read and organized.Mostly clear.Some parts confusing.Difficult to understand.
